_comment: Processes confirmed to leak handles. pcdoctor names them in 'check' and 'leaks'. Add yours with a pull request or an issue (pcdoctor report). Kernel drivers that keep exited processes in memory are listed in https://github.com/marloncodess/claude-code-zombies/blob/main/known-culprits.json

handleLeaks.device: RZ608 Wi-Fi 6E / Bluetooth adapter (MediaTek MT7921, often sold as AMD RZ608)
handleLeaks.rate: 0 to 760,000 handles per hour, in bursts; 2.2 million system handles after 29 h uptime
handleLeaks.evidence: pcdoctor handles mtkbtsvc: 96,002 of 96,088 handles are Event objects; restarting the service drops it from 464,317 to 222 handles; growth is unrelated to process starts (0 new handles during 439 extra starts)
handleLeaks.fix: Update the Bluetooth driver from your mainboard or laptop vendor. Until then: pcdoctor watchdog install mtkbtsvc (restarts the service, Bluetooth devices drop for a few seconds).
